correctness.rationale: Every prism vertex has degree three, so with at most one initial blue vertex no source has exactly one white neighbor. For exactly two initially blue vertices a first legal skew force requires the pair to share a neighbor; because the odd prism with n≥5 is triangle-free, this is precisely a distance-two pair. Up to rotation/reflection/layer exchange there are same-layer (0,0),(2,0) and cross-layer (0,0),(1,1) seed types. Explicit constructive forced stage alternates layers and advances in two directions, coloring all vertices; the cross-layer seed first forces a vertex yielding the successful same-layer seed. All 4n types succeed. They are edges of 4-regular connected distance-two graph H_n, giving line-graph exchange 6-regular with 12n edges. A slide fixing v requires an edge within its four distance-two neighbors; such a pair exists only for n=5, between the two same-layer distance-two neighbors, giving 2C₅ plus isolates. Independent skew-rule enumeration all blue pairs for odd n=5..17 reproduced the 4n classification, exchange/sliding edge counts, and n=5 exception. Finite enumeration corroborates the explicit all-odd-n proof.
